claim_ceiling: This experiment measures comparative negative-control discovery behavior between two exact frozen candidate prompts under one provider/model and one small frozen synthetic corpus. It does not establish semantic correctness, zero false-positive probability, production readiness, institutional admission, authority, enforceability, legal interpretation, cross-model generalization, statistical equivalence, or independent validation.
experiment_kind: paired A/B falsification over frozen negative controls
false_positive_definition: normative_expected is false AND the response survived the existing candidate boundary AND candidate_count > 0. A boundary rejection is not a false positive because it did not survive the boundary; a provider error is not a false positive because no response was observed.
purpose: Determine whether the single CSEM-031 false-positive observation in the live OIC-CANDIDATE-SEMANTICS-004 characterization is ordinary provider variance or evidence that the 004 framing-separation prompt weakened normative-vs-non-normative discovery. Every source text is carried byte-identical from the frozen 003 corpus: the question is whether behaviour changed against an already frozen negative-control set, so the set itself must not move.
